pr.title: Apply `EarlyOtherwiseBranch` to scalar value
pr.description:
In the future, I'm thinking of hoisting discriminant via GVN so that we only need to write very little code here.

r? @cjgillot
pr.author: dianqk

analysis.summary: EarlyOtherwiseBranch was extended from hoisting enum-discriminant computations to also folding nested scalar matches (e.g. `match (x, y) { (1,1)=>..., (2,2)=>..., (3,3)=>..., _=>... }`). For a child block with no statements whose `SwitchInt` directly tests `Operand::Copy(place)`, the pass now hoists `Ne(parent, child)` before the parent switch; for the existing discriminant case it still hoists `Rvalue::Discriminant`. Correctness depends on same-typed places, exact one-to-one matching of inner/outer switch values, `Copy` (not `Move`) for the scalar operand, and preserving the old UB guard for discriminant hoisting.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `evaluate_candidate` only recognized a child block of the form `bb: { _d = discriminant(place); switchInt(move _d) -> [v: ...]; }`. It required the child block to have exactly one statement assigning `Rvalue::Discriminant(child_place)` to a local, terminated by `SwitchInt { discr: Operand::Move(discr_local) }`. The pass then created a second-discriminant temp and compared it with the already-computed parent discriminant. It always required the parent's `otherwise` block to be `empty_unreachable` because hoisting a discriminant computation can compute the discriminant of an invalid enum value: "Hoisting the `discriminant(Q)` out of the `A` arm causes us to compute the discriminant of an invalid value, which is UB." Scalar child switches on `Operand::Copy(place)` with zero statements were not matched, so `opt5` remained as nested switches.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The new rewrite must not be applied merely because the outer switch value reaches a child switch. An over-broad scalar extension that hoists `Ne(parent, child)` and bypasses the inner switch without requiring the child block to have zero statements, without requiring `switch_op == Operand::Copy(place)`, without requiring `child_ty == parent_ty`, and without requiring `target_value == value` would miscompile `opt5_failed`: outer value `3` reaches an inner switch on `2`, so the `(3,2)` arm returns `6` originally; folding on `x == y` would send `(3,2)` to the otherwise value `0` (and an ill-typed fold would compare `u32` with `u64` in `opt5_failed_type`). The shipped pass instead rejects these via `if child_ty != parent_ty { return None; }`, `if *switch_op != Operand::Copy(place) { return false; }`, and `target_value == value`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR for nested `match`es over a same-typed scalar pair, e.g. `match (x: u32, y: u32) { (1,1)=>4, (2,2)=>5, (3,3)=>6, _=>0 }`, plus the analogous enum-discriminant shape. The outer `SwitchInt` tests one place, each outer arm's child block either contains one `Rvalue::Discriminant(place)` statement or zero statements and tests the other place directly with `Operand::Copy`, and each child switch has exactly one matched value plus an otherwise target equal to the chosen destination.
analysis.trigger: A parent `SwitchInt` dispatches to child blocks that each switch on the other component of a same-typed pair with the same corresponding constants, so the two-level dispatch can be collapsed into one equality/`Ne` test plus the parent switch.
preconditions: `child_ty == parent_ty`; the patch keeps `if child_ty != parent_ty { return None; }`.
Child block has at most one statement: `let need_hoist_discriminant = bbs[child].statements.len() == 1;`.

Scalar/no-hoist path: child block has no statements and `switch_op == Operand::Copy(place)`, enforced by `if !branch.statements.is_empty() { return false; }` and `if *switch_op != Operand::Copy(place) { return false; }`.

Discriminant path: exactly one `StatementKind::Assign(box (discr_place, Rvalue::Discriminant(from_place)))` with `from_place == place`, `discr_place.projection.is_empty()`, and `switch_op == Operand::Move(discr_place)`.
Each outer-target child falls through to the chosen `destination`: `if destination != targets.otherwise() { return false; }`.

Each child switch has exactly one matched value and that value equals the outer value: `let (Some((target_value, _)), None) = (iter.next(), iter.next()) else { return false; }; target_value == value`.
When hoisting a discriminant, the parent otherwise must still be empty/unreachable: `if !bbs[targets.otherwise()].is_empty_unreachable() { ... return None; }`.

Destination selection: `let destination = if need_hoist_discriminant || bbs[targets.otherwise()].is_empty_unreachable()` ... else `targets.otherwise()`; so the scalar case keeps the original parent otherwise when it is reachable.
pitfalls: Do not apply the scalar fold when the inner matched constant differs from the outer value. `opt5_failed` deliberately uses `(3, 2) => 6`; the test asserts `// CHECK-NOT: Ne(`.
Do not fold places of different types. `opt5_failed_type` uses `x: u32, y: u64` and also asserts `// CHECK-NOT: Ne(`.
The scalar path requires `Operand::Copy(place)`, not `Operand::Move(place)`; a move would invalidate the place before the hoisted comparison and is a separate restriction from the type check.

The UB guard is only relaxed for the no-hoist scalar path. Copying/comparing a scalar is safe, but hoisting `Rvalue::Discriminant` can compute the discriminant of an invalid enum value, so the old `empty_unreachable` requirement must remain for discriminant hoisting.

Destination selection is not always `child_targets.otherwise()`: when hoisting is not needed and the parent otherwise is reachable, it must be `targets.otherwise()`; otherwise unequal values could be routed to the wrong block.
Do not require the scalar child block to contain a discriminant assignment: it must have zero statements, while the discriminant path must have exactly one.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR dump tests with `// EMIT_MIR early_otherwise_branch.opt5.EarlyOtherwiseBranch.diff` and CHECK-LABEL/CHECK/CHECK-NOT. Positive: `opt5` on `match (x: u32, y: u32) { (1,1)=>4, (2,2)=>5, (3,3)=>6, _=>0 }` must show `_6 = Ne(copy (_3.0: u32), copy (_3.1: u32));`, `switchInt(move _6) -> [0: bb6, otherwise: bb1];`, and the collapsed parent switch in bb6. Negative controls: `opt5_failed` with `(3,2)=>6` and `opt5_failed_type(x: u32, y: u64)` must both preserve the nested switches and satisfy `// CHECK-NOT: Ne(`. Also keep the existing runtime `main` calls as a smoke test, but do not claim execution/reproduction. Add analogous MIR tests for a non-`Copy`/`Move` child switch and for differing child-vs-parent otherwise destinations.
